items.title: Scourge of Princes: Army Builder
items.summary: Vexillia built basic and advanced army-list spreadsheets for Scourge of Princes. The sheets check artillery and formation limits as you build a force, making it easier to compare two plausible Italian Wars armies before setting up a game.

items.title: The Attack on Breville-les-Monts, 11th June 1944
items.summary: Neil W’s 10mm O Group scenario sends the Black Watch against two built-up areas east of the Orne. One company starts at Château Saint-Côme, so it’s a ready-made example of how to represent a historical flank position without scripting the attack.

items.title: Teeny Tiny WW2
items.summary: A 2mm Hürtgen Forest game pits a US rifle company against machine-gun positions around a wooded hill. The report shows how resolving fire before movement makes suppression matter even on a table with no tanks.

items.title: The Battle of Wittenberg, 2nd October 1760 (The Scenario)
items.summary: A Seven Years War scenario for Tricorn gives the outnumbered Prussians a defensible position and the Reichsarmee the challenge of bringing its strength to bear. The map, deployments, and historical background show how to turn a lopsided battle into a playable one.

items.title: Battle of Lal 2444BC
items.summary: A Mesopotamian tabletop pursuit comes down to two canal crossings and a hill the army of Ur must hold on turn 13. The report shows how terrain gives chariots, spearmen, and light bowmen distinct jobs.

items.title: Italy 1943 - I Haven't The Foggia'st - Monty's Casino Campaign Turn 1
items.summary: A British advance off the Foggia plain opens a 1943 mini-campaign. One reconnaissance unit works around the flank while the main force attacks a rocky outcrop, giving the game two linked problems on the same table.

items.title: The Battle of Monocacy After Action Report – Unioncon 2026!
items.summary: For a Monocacy convention game, the host shapes hills with foam under a mat and lays the rivers and roads on top. The Union gets freedom to redeploy, and the players’ decision to defend forward turns the two bridges into the focus of the game.

imageRights.alt: Miniature armies on the Monocacy convention table.

items.title: Raiders of the Malta Convoys: 1941
items.summary: This convention scenario starts on a Mediterranean search map and zooms into a cruiser and destroyer action when the fleets meet. The author explains how Nimitz and Halsey keep convoy hunting and surface combat moving in the same session.

items.title: The Battle of Mohacs, 1526
items.summary: An Art de la Guerre v4 scenario for Mohács puts Ottoman artillery on a rise above the Danube and makes marsh and a rough stream part of the approach. It offers an eastern counterpart to Italian Wars scenarios from the same generation.

items.title: Sahel Conflicts: Civilian Vehicles
items.summary: A modeling project for games set in Mali uses printed civilian vehicles to give the table a sense of place. Light dust, local registration plates, and a Bamako minibus help the cars read as civilian traffic alongside military vehicles.

items.title: Walk like an Egyptian, putting paint on Wargames Atlantic's 28mm Egyptian Infantry
items.summary: A test build of Wargames Atlantic’s 28mm Egyptian infantry turns into a whole painted box. The author compares how archers and spearmen look on bases for Midgard, and explains why painting shields on the sprue would have made the job easier.

items.title: Viking Raid on Iona Abbey- Scenario Rules
items.summary: An abbey raid for Little Wars TV’s Ravenfeast includes downloadable scenario and force sheets. The author ran it six times at conventions and identifies the fort and ship positions that matter if you adapt it to another coast or collection.

imageRights.alt: Tabletop terrain and deployment for the Iona Abbey raid.

items.title: Big Muddy Historical Gaming Alliance – St. Louis November Game Day West Command Con Lite Hampton Roads
items.summary: A St. Louis club’s alternate Hampton Roads engagement brings the Norfolk and James River squadrons in on different schedules. Card-driven movement and slower gunnery give smaller vessels time to influence the game alongside the ironclads.

items.title: Du mont Suribachi aux côteaux de la Marne: Iwo Jima 3D
items.summary: This French-language photo report shows a three-dimensional Memoir ’44 table with a fortified Mount Suribachi, hidden Japanese positions, and a buried tank. The narrow finish makes the airfield’s value as a victory objective easy to see.

items.title: Communal Italians
items.summary: A Communal Italian DBA army takes shape around a carroccio, crossbowmen, and spear blocks. The author shows how a few alternate bases let the same Essex collection field a German ally or change the mix of Italian troops.

items.title: A Back of Beyond and WW2 Chinese Company some thoughts
items.source: You Do Not Know the North
items.summary: The author builds a Chinese Communist rifle company and weighs which mortars and machine guns belong in a given game. It’s a hobbyist’s look at how equipment availability can make two companies with similar structures play differently.

items.title: Warlord Epic Scale Zulus
items.summary: A close look at Warlord’s Epic Scale Zulu sprue shows how different group sizes can create either dense formations or open skirmish lines. It’s a useful visual reference for making a massed army readable on a smaller footprint.

items.title: Siege of Tobruk
items.source: 20mm Crimean War Wargaming and Other Stuff
items.summary: An enlarged Command and Colors map becomes an 8-by-4-foot Tobruk table with 3-inch hexes. The setup shows how the ditch, minefields, strongpoints, and armoured reserve fit together before the first turn.

items.title: Ship construction and fitting out
items.summary: A 1/700 fleet-building update mixes kits, conversions, scratch-built ships, and printed carriers. The author shows what gets painted before the flight decks go on, and how one cruiser model can stand in for several related ships.

items.title: Ship Happens, Part X 1/600 Warrior and some ACW ironclads
items.summary: A batch of 1/600 American Civil War ironclads shares the workbench with a resin HMS Warrior. The author explains how a little standing rigging helps support the print’s fragile masts and shows how the British warship differs visually from its American contemporaries.
